text:
maria: FYI we just got an automated alert from Trivy -> libssl (OpenSSL) 3.x CVE chain, flagged in several alpine-slim base images. low->high severity mix.
ashwin: Can you paste the Trivy output? which tags are affected?
maria: snippet below, found in alpine:3.18-slim and our internal slim-build:latest image.
```
VULN: CVE-2026-XXXX (HIGH)
Package: libcrypto3
Installed: 3.0.8-r0
Fixed-In: 3.0.10-r0
Path: /usr/local/bin/app -> /lib/libcrypto.so.3
```
julia: thanks. Are Ubuntu-based images showing the same CVE or just Alpine?
maria: Ubuntu focal/base images show a related glibc-cve but not identical. different packages. main risk is libcrypto regression on arm64 minimal images.
tomas: quick risk triage: is this exploitable in our runtime? we don't expose TLS from containers directly, but some services do make outbound TLS calls using system libs. Also some language runtimes bundle OpenSSL.
nashwin: we should treat HIGH CVE as P0 for rebuild if exploitability plausible. propose plan: 1) reproduce CVE hit in a container, 2) build patched base image (alpine:3.18 + libcrypto 3.0.10), 3) run unit + smoke tests, 4) canary deploy to non-prod, 5) sign + promote.
maria: agree. also need to update SBOM and CVE tracker ticket. I'll open the ticket.
sec-bot: New issue created: SEC-5821 - libcrypto (OpenSSL 3.x) in alpine-slim images. Assigned to maria.
nashwin: CI changes: add build job to create `alpine-slim:3.18-patched-2026-03-20` and multi-arch manifests. ensure qemu emulation for arm64 test matrix.
ci-bot: CI pipeline triggered: image-rebuild-patch-1799901111. Logs: building amd64, arm64.
maria: test checklist draft: - run `trivy image` on patched image - run internal integration test suite (http, grpc, model load) - run perf microbenchmarks (latency P50/P95) - smoke test streaming API - verify image signing with cosign - update SBOM & push to artifact registry - update canary rollout policy to 5% for 24h then 25% if no regressions.
julia: what about Ubuntu images? can we patch instead of rebuild full image? backport may be available via apt security. I'd prefer backport for larger base images to avoid regressions.
nashwin: for Ubuntu we should prefer distro patch/backport (apt update + apt upgrade libssl) and rebuild base image layers that depend on it. keep image digests for reproducibility.
tomas: regression concern: historically OpenSSL minor bumps caused language binding issues (python ssl, node native addons). plan: run language compatibility matrix: python 3.10, node 18, go 1.20. Also run our fuzzing harness on binary.
maria: good call. I'll mark language tests as gate for canary.
nashwin: rollout schedule proposal: - t+0h: push patched images to staging registry - t+2h: run full test matrix - t+6h: sign + create manifest - t+8h: canary 5% on staging services - t+32h: expand 25% if clean - t+72h: full prod promotion.
julia: add notification to support & customer success if we change public image tags or if any services see restarts.
maria: done. I'll open SEC-5821 checklist and add owners. Also we should add a small log grep to detect any runtime `SSL_*` symbol errors in canary logs.
sec-bot: Reminder: add SBOM field `patch_level` and `cve_fingerprint` for traceability.
maria: question: do we need to sign the image with our HSM-backed key or is cosign with KMS ok? security policy prefers KMS-wrapped cosign key for production images.
nashwin: KMS-wrapped cosign key. I'll handle KMS grants for the CI service account. need 2 engineers to have cosign key access for emergency revocation procedures.
tomas: don't forget to update docs/ops/runbooks with rollback steps: `docker pull OLD_DIGEST && k8s set image --record` etc. keep old digest available for 7 days.
julia: once patch is live, update internal vulnerability dashboard and close Sec ticket with postmortem note. include perf numbers.
maria: I'll run the rebuild now and post results. tagging @eng-oncall in case canary trips alerts. :pray:
ci-bot: Build finished (amd64): success. (arm64 still running)
ci-bot: Build finished (arm64): success. Artifact URI: registry.internal/redwood/alpine-slim:3.18-patched-2026-03-20@sha256:abcdef
maria: Trivy on new image: no libcrypto CVEs found, glibc CVE still present in ubuntu variants (separate ticket). Perf quickcheck: P95 latency +0.8% (within tolerance).
nashwin: good to proceed with staged canary. I'll update the canary policy and start rollout in 10m.
maria: starting canary, will monitor errors, cpu, latency, and ssl-related logs. ping if anything off.
omas: (typo) -- monitoring
sec-bot: Canary metrics: errors spike +0.2% (within noise), no SSL symbol errors.
julia: looks clean. proceed to 25% in 24h if no regressions.
maria: closing loop: will add postmortem and link SEC-5821 to the public regression tracker. thanks everyone.
